nodes.description: Balanced energy-appropriate nutrition and regular physical activity are the foundation of care. Treat detected dysglycemia with standard agents such as metformin or insulin and dyslipidemia with statins, fibrates, or omega-3 therapy as clinically indicated. In selected patients, off-label thiazolidinedione therapy may improve metabolic complications, but evidence is for partial lipodystrophy broadly rather than classic APL and regional fat excess can increase. This manages complications but does not regrow lost adipose tissue or arrest the complement process.

Metreleptin therapy is effective for metabolic complications in hypoleptinemic patients with generalized lipodystrophy and selected patients with partial lipodystrophy. Other treatments not specific for lipodystrophy may be helpful as well (eg, metformin for diabetes, and statins or fibrates for hyperlipidemia).

nodes.description: Metreleptin is a recombinant leptin analogue for selected patients with severe metabolic complications despite standard therapy. In the EU, Myalepta is authorized for confirmed partial lipodystrophy, including Barraquer-Simons syndrome, from age 12 after standard treatments fail. The current US label is limited to generalized lipodystrophy and states that safety and effectiveness in partial lipodystrophy are not established. APL-specific efficacy remains uncertain because published cohorts combine partial-lipodystrophy subtypes; treatment does not restore fat distribution.
